from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
from datetime import datetime

app = FastAPI()

class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str
    created_at: datetime
    password_hash: str
    internal_notes: str

@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=User)
def get_user(user_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()

A client requests a user; the response includes password_hash and internal_notes unnecessarily. What happens?
options: Sensitive fields returned; security & bandwidth waste
Response size doubled; network latency increased
explanation: Response model should use a separate Pydantic model excluding sensitive fields; return response_model=UserPublic to control output.

options: Immediately; lru_cache invalidates on file changes
After server restart or manual cache clear
explanation: lru_cache has no TTL; changes aren't reflected until cache is cleared or server restarts; use external cache with TTL or reload on demand.
OFFSET requires scanning past 999990 rows before reading the 10 requested; use keyset pagination (WHERE id > last_id) for better performance on large offsets.

options: Data generated on-demand; reduces initial response time
Prevents buffering; client receives data as generated
explanation: StreamingResponse allows partial data to reach client immediately; client starts processing while server generates rest, reducing time-to-first-byte.

options: Loads all users into memory; counts in Python
Makes N database queries where N is user count
Uses correct SQL count() function efficiently
explanation: loads all user rows into ORM objects, then counts in Python; use db.query(func.count(User.id)).scalar() instead for single COUNT query.

options: 1 (cache hit on second request after first completes)
explanation: Without cache locks, both concurrent requests see cache miss simultaneously and both execute the function; use aiocache's lock support.
GZipMiddleware compresses text responses; JSON with repeated data compresses ~80-90%; client needs Accept-Encoding: gzip header.

from fastapi import FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.orm import joinedload
from sqlalchemy import select

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/authors/{author_id}/books")
def get_author_books(author_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    author = db.query(Author).options(
        joinedload(Author.books)
    ).filter(Author.id == author_id).first()
    return author

Compared to loading Author then separately loading books, what improvement is this?
options: 1 JOIN query instead of 2 separate queries
explanation: joinedload() performs one JOIN query instead of N+1 (1 for author + 1 per book); eliminates lazy-load queries triggered when accessing author.books.

options: FastAPI serves static files slowly; use CDN
File served from memory buffer; no streaming
FastAPI processes request through full middleware chain
explanation: Static files still go through FastAPI middleware (auth, logging, etc.); for production, use web server (Nginx) or CDN to serve static files bypassing FastAPI.

options: Entire payload buffered in memory before validation
Request body discarded after route matching
explanation: Pydantic must validate full model tree before returning; large payloads are buffered entirely in memory; use streaming or chunk processing for huge requests.
